stem: A 24-year-old woman has had fever and lower abdominal pain for 2 days. Temperature is 38.6 C, and pelvic examination shows purulent cervical discharge and cervical motion tenderness. Pregnancy test is negative. Two weeks ago she had a contraceptive method placed during a clinic visit. She hopes to have children in her mid-30s.
oneliner: 24F + 2 d fever, lower abdominal pain + purulent cervical discharge, cervical motion tenderness + negative pregnancy test + contraceptive method placed 2 wk ago → which method?
ask: Which contraceptive method most likely contributed to this problem?

whyNot.A: **Pills**: do not pass through the cervix; they lower the risk of PID
whyNot.B: Placed under the **skin of the arm**; no route to the pelvis

why: **Fever, cervical motion tenderness and purulent discharge soon after placement** = pelvic inflammatory disease. An **IUD** carries a small risk of PID in the first weeks, and untreated PID can scar the tubes and cause infertility.

drug.name: Copper IUD
drug.how: Copper is spermicidal and causes a sterile inflammatory reaction that prevents implantation
drug.use: Long-acting contraception; emergency contraception within 5 days
drug.watch: Heavier, more painful periods; PID in the weeks after insertion; uterine perforation; ectopic pregnancy if it fails

stem: A 38-year-old woman smokes 10 cigarettes a day and wants contraception. She has mild intermittent asthma, a BMI of 31, drinks wine once a week, and her mother has osteoporosis. Her blood pressure is 122/78 mm Hg. She asks about the combined estrogen-progestin pill.
oneliner: 38F + smokes 10 cigarettes/day + mild asthma + BMI 31 + wine weekly + mother with osteoporosis + BP 122/78 + asks about the combined pill → what is the main reason against it?
ask: Which of her features is the strongest reason to avoid the combined pill?

whyNot.D: A **relative** concern at most; much weaker than smoking at 38

answer: Smoking at age 35 or older (combined oral contraceptive thrombosis risk)
why: **Smoking at 35 or older + estrogen** sharply raises the risk of **venous and arterial thrombosis**, including MI and stroke. Choose a progestin-only or non-hormonal method.

drug.name: Combined oral contraceptive
drug.how: Suppresses ovulation (LH surge), thickens cervical mucus, thins the endometrium
drug.watch: Venous thromboembolism, stroke and MI (smokers over 35), hypertension, hepatic adenoma; contraindicated with migraine with aura

stem: A 22-year-old man who is a varsity athlete has had worsening acne on his back and face for 2 months, along with ankle swelling and itching. His blood pressure and fasting glucose are normal, his hands and jaw have not changed in size, and he has no breast tissue enlargement. Alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin are mildly raised, and ultrasound shows a normal biliary tree. He admits he takes a supplement to gain muscle mass.
oneliner: 22M athlete + 2 mo acne + ankle edema, itching + mild cholestasis, normal biliary tree + normal BP and glucose + taking a muscle-building supplement → which substance?
ask: Which of the following substances is he most likely taking?

whyNot.A: **Acromegalic changes** (larger hands and jaw) would appear; they have not
whyNot.B: **Glucocorticoid excess** raises blood pressure and glucose; both are normal
whyNot.C: **Estrogen** is not a muscle-building aid and does not cause acne in men
whyNot.D: Would raise cortisol, so **hypertension and hyperglycemia**; both are normal

why: **Muscle-building supplement + acne + fluid retention + cholestasis** = anabolic steroid. The 17-alpha-alkylated oral forms like **methandrostenolone** cause **cholestatic liver injury**, acne and **salt and water retention**.

drug.name: Anabolic androgenic steroids (methandrostenolone)
drug.how: Activate androgen receptors to build muscle; oral 17-alpha-alkylated forms are hepatotoxic
drug.use: Delayed puberty, wasting states, hypogonadism (abuse for muscle mass)
drug.watch: Acne, fluid retention, cholestasis, testicular atrophy, gynecomastia, aggression, low HDL

stem: A 29-year-old man and his wife have been unable to conceive for 2 years. He is a competitive bodybuilder with a very muscular build and has used a weekly injectable supplement for muscle mass for the past year. Both testes are small and soft. Semen analysis shows no sperm. He has no history of mumps or radiation exposure.
oneliner: 29M bodybuilder + 2 y infertility + weekly injected muscle supplement 1 y + small soft testes + azoospermia → why infertile?
ask: Which of the following best explains his infertility?

options.A: Increased conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone
options.B: Increased aromatization of testosterone in fat
options.C: Cholestatic liver injury lowering sperm production
options.E: Negative feedback lowering pituitary LH and FSH

whyNot.A: Raises **DHT** in the skin and prostate; does not shut off the testes
whyNot.C: Liver injury does not account for **atrophic testes** with no sperm
whyNot.D: GH does not suppress gonadotropins and does not explain **small testes with azoospermia**

answer: Suppressed LH and FSH from negative feedback by exogenous androgen
why: **Injected androgen + small soft testes + azoospermia** = exogenous testosterone shutting off the axis. High circulating androgen **inhibits GnRH, LH and FSH**, so the testes **lose Leydig and Sertoli cell stimulation**, shrink, and stop making sperm.

drug.name: Testosterone / anabolic steroids
drug.how: Activate androgen receptors; excess gives negative feedback on hypothalamus and pituitary
drug.use: Hypogonadism, delayed puberty (abuse for muscle mass)
drug.watch: Testicular atrophy, infertility, gynecomastia, acne, polycythemia, low HDL

stem: A 60-year-old woman has had postcoital vaginal bleeding for 3 weeks. Pelvic examination shows a firm mass on the anterior upper vaginal wall, and biopsy shows clear cell adenocarcinoma. Her mother says that during her pregnancy in the 1960s she took a daily medication after two earlier miscarriages.
oneliner: 60F + 3 wk postcoital bleeding + anterior upper vaginal mass + clear cell adenocarcinoma + mother took a pregnancy drug in the 1960s after miscarriages → which drug?
ask: Which of the following drugs did her mother most likely take?

whyNot.A: Natural hormone with **no known carcinogenic effect** on the fetal vagina
whyNot.C: **Beta-2 agonist** for preterm labor; not linked to vaginal cancer
whyNot.E: **Beta-2 agonist** tocolytic; not linked to vaginal cancer

why: **Clear cell adenocarcinoma of the vagina + maternal drug to prevent miscarriage** = in utero **diethylstilbestrol** exposure. It also causes uterine anomalies (T-shaped uterus) and vaginal adenosis.

drug.name: Diethylstilbestrol
drug.how: Activates estrogen receptors; it was given in pregnancy to prevent miscarriage
drug.watch: In daughters: vaginal clear cell adenocarcinoma, vaginal adenosis, T-shaped uterus, infertility

stem: A 30-year-old woman asks for a combined pill containing ethinyl estradiol. She has a monthly migraine that is preceded by flashing lights in her visual field. She has well-controlled asthma, drinks a glass of wine most evenings, and her grandmother had breast cancer at 72. She does not smoke, has a BMI of 28, and her blood pressure is normal.
oneliner: 30F + requests combined ethinyl estradiol pill + migraine with visual aura + controlled asthma, light alcohol, grandmother with breast cancer + non-smoker, BMI 28, normal BP → which feature is a problem?
ask: Which feature of her history makes this pill unsafe?

whyNot.A: Asthma does not interact with estrogen; the danger here is **stroke and clot risk**
whyNot.B: Light drinking is not a bar to the pill; **active liver disease** would be
whyNot.D: A **distant family history** does not bar the pill; **her own** estrogen-dependent cancer would
whyNot.E: Overweight is not a contraindication; **uncontrolled hypertension** would be

answer: Migraine with aura raises stroke risk with estrogen
why: **Estrogen raises clotting factors** and stroke risk, and **migraine with aura** is itself linked to ischemic stroke, so the combination is avoided. Other bars include **prior venous thromboembolism, estrogen-dependent cancer, active liver disease and uncontrolled hypertension**.

drug.name: Ethinyl estradiol with a progestin (combined oral contraceptive)
drug.how: Negative feedback suppresses GnRH, FSH and LH, blocking ovulation; estrogen also raises hepatic clotting factor synthesis
drug.use: Contraception, dysmenorrhea, heavy periods, acne and hirsutism in PCOS
drug.watch: Venous thromboembolism, stroke, hypertension, hepatic adenoma; contraindicated in migraine with aura

idea.rule: Estrogen-containing pills are avoided when there is a clot, stroke or estrogen-dependent tumor risk.
also: History of DVT or pulmonary embolism
Breast cancer or other estrogen-sensitive cancer
Active liver disease or liver tumor

stem: A 62-year-old postmenopausal woman with osteoporosis is started on raloxifene. Her physician warns about a specific serious adverse effect and tells her to seek urgent care for a swollen calf or sudden shortness of breath.
oneliner: 62F + postmenopausal osteoporosis + starts raloxifene + told to report calf swelling or sudden dyspnea → which adverse effect?
ask: Which serious adverse effect is she being warned about?

whyNot.A: Seen with **tamoxifen**, which stimulates the uterus; raloxifene **blocks** estrogen there
whyNot.B: Raloxifene acts like estrogen in **bone** and **protects** it
whyNot.C: A **potassium-sparing diuretic or ACE-inhibitor** effect, unrelated to SERMs
whyNot.D: Seen with **vincristine, isoniazid or platinum agents**, not SERMs

why: **Raloxifene and tamoxifen** are SERMs that act like **estrogen in the liver**, raising clotting factors and **venous thromboembolism**. The warning for **leg swelling or sudden dyspnea** points to DVT and pulmonary embolism.

drug.name: Raloxifene
drug.how: Estrogen agonist in bone and liver, antagonist in breast and uterus
drug.use: Postmenopausal osteoporosis, breast cancer risk reduction
drug.watch: Venous thromboembolism, hot flashes, leg cramps

idea.rule: A SERM acts as estrogen in some tissues and blocks it in others, so it carries estrogen's clot risk.
also: Tamoxifen also raises endometrial cancer risk
Raloxifene does not stimulate the endometrium

stem: A 64-year-old man with angina uses sublingual nitroglycerin for chest pain. He asks his physician about sildenafil for erectile dysfunction. The physician refuses to prescribe it and explains the danger of using both drugs on the same day.
oneliner: 64M + angina on sublingual nitroglycerin + asks for sildenafil for ED → which adverse effect is feared?
ask: What serious adverse effect is the physician worried about?

whyNot.A: Feared with **ACE inhibitors or potassium-sparing diuretics**, not with nitrate plus PDE5 inhibitor
whyNot.C: He takes **no beta blocker**; sildenafil does not slow the heart
whyNot.D: Not the dangerous interaction with a **nitrate**
whyNot.E: A rare effect of drugs like **clozapine**, not of sildenafil

why: **Nitrates and sildenafil both increase cGMP** (nitrates by releasing NO, sildenafil by blocking its breakdown through **PDE5 inhibition**). Together they produce **profound vasodilation and hypotension**, so the combination is contraindicated.

drug.name: Sildenafil
drug.how: Blocks cGMP breakdown, prolonging nitric-oxide-mediated smooth muscle relaxation in the corpus cavernosum
drug.watch: Severe hypotension with nitrates, headache, flushing, blue-tinged vision, priapism

idea.rule: Two drugs that both raise cGMP can drop blood pressure dangerously.
also: Sildenafil effects: headache, flushing, blue-tinged vision

stem: A 27-year-old weightlifter has noticed tender breast tissue under both nipples over several months. He admits to injecting a synthetic androgen to gain muscle. He has acne and small, soft testes. Prolactin and the rest of his examination are unremarkable.
oneliner: 27M + weightlifter on injected androgen + tender bilateral subareolar tissue + acne + small testes → which process explains the breasts?
ask: Which process most likely explains the breast enlargement?

options.B: Prolactin excess from a pituitary adenoma
options.C: A defect in the androgen receptor
options.D: Liver failure with reduced estrogen clearance
options.E: hCG secreted by a testicular tumor

whyNot.B: His **prolactin is normal**, and there is no galactorrhea or visual symptom
whyNot.C: His breasts grew only **after he began injecting**, and his **acne** shows his androgen receptors respond
whyNot.D: No **stigmata of liver disease**; the cause is the drug he injects
whyNot.E: A tumor would give a **testicular mass**; his testes are small and soft

answer: Peripheral aromatization of androgens to estradiol
why: Excess androgen is **converted by aromatase in fat to estradiol**, which stimulates breast tissue. The same steroids suppress LH, causing **testicular atrophy**, and the result is **gynecomastia**.

drug.name: Testosterone and synthetic anabolic androgens
drug.how: Androgen receptor agonists; excess is aromatized to estradiol and suppresses LH and FSH by negative feedback
drug.watch: Gynecomastia, testicular atrophy, infertility, acne, erythrocytosis, liver tumors

idea.rule: A high androgen load is partly converted to estrogen, and the estrogen causes the breast growth.
also: Negative feedback suppresses LH and FSH
Gynecomastia also from spironolactone, ketoconazole and cimetidine
